sentences.text: It is submitted that one Kashinath a Civil Contractor was forcibly laying the road on the instruction of the respondent-authorities encroaching upon the land belonging to the petitioner without acquiring the same.
Petitioner had preferred a suit in O.S.No.31/2019 before the Civil Judge & JMFC, Afzalpur.
By the judgment and decree dated 20.12.2024, the suit came to be decreed declaring that the laying of the road in the land bearing Sy.No.76/4 and Sy.No.76/6 belonging to the petitioner was illegal.
Based on which, the petitioner made a representation dated 30.09.2025 to the respondents requiring them to initiate the acquisition proceedings.
However, the same has not been considered.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the respondent-authorities have no justification to utilize NC: 2025:KHC-K:7415 HC-KAR the property of the petitioner for the purpose of laying the road without paying the compensation.
Hence, seeks for direction to consider the representation.

4. Learned Additional Government Advocate submits that the case of the petitioner will be considered in accordance with law and the compensation as payable under the law will be determined, given some time in the matter.
5. Heard.
Perused the records.

6. Relevant at this juncture to refer the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Kolkata Municipal Corporation and another vs. Bimal Kumar Shah and another - (2024) 10 SCC 533, wherein at paragraph 30 the Apex Court has held as under :
"30.

sentences.text: What then are these sub-rights or strands of this swadeshi constitutional fabric constituting the right to property?
Seven such sub-rights can be identified, albeit non-exhaustive.

These are:
i) The duty of the State to inform the person that it intends to acquire his property - the right to notice, NC: 2025:KHC-K:7415 HC-KAR ii) The duty of the State to hear objections to the acquisition-the right to be heard,
iii) The duty of the State to inform the person of its decision to acquire-the right to a reasoned decision,
iv) The duty of the State to demonstrate that the acquisition is for public purpose-the duty to acquire only for public purpose,
v) The duty of the State to restitute and rehabilitate - the right of restitution or fair compensation,
vi) The duty of the State to conduct the process of acquisition efficiently and within prescribed timelines of the proceedings-the right to an efficient and expeditious process, and Lal Ahmed vs The Deputy Commissioner on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171730099/
3 vii) The final conclusion of the proceedings leading to vesting - the right of conclusion."
7. In view of the above, the petition is allowed.
8. The respondent-authorities shall initiate the proceedings for acquisition of land belonging to the petitioner.
9. Respondent-authorities shall conclude the acquisition process and determine the compensation with all statutory benefits permissible under the applicable law NC: 2025:KHC-K:7415 HC-KAR and same shall be determined within an outer limit of six months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
